SV-10002.title: Global Search: a customer cannot be found by their postcode
SV-10002.description: A customer's postcode is printed on their record, and the search box ignores it. Anyone who knows roughly where a customer is - which is how people tell two similar company names apart - has no way to reach them from the search box. On the version people use today, typing the postcode brings the customer straight back.
steps: Sign in to the new version on the test branch: https://sv9160.qa.shopview.com

Click the search box at the top of the screen (or press Ctrl and K), type ZZAUTOTEST Bridgeport Hauling, and open that customer from the Customers group. This also shows the search box itself is working.
On the customer's page, read the postcode under Address. It is 44872-9931.
Open the search box again and type that postcode exactly as the record prints it.
Wait for the results and read the Customers group.
current: Nothing comes back at all. The panel reads "No results for 44872-9931" and every group shows nought.
The same customer comes straight back when their name is typed, so the record is there and the search box is working.
expected: The customer whose postcode was typed is returned, under Customers.
This is what the version people use today does.
SV-10002.shot_caption: The same postcode typed into both versions. Above, the live product returns the customer. Below, the new version returns nothing.
SV-10002.sources:
The expected behaviour comes from the version people use today. It was not read out of a specification - it was typed into the live product at https://app.shopview.com on 15 September 2026, where the postcode 44872-9931 returned the customer ZZAUTOTEST Bridgeport Hauling, and the picture above is that search. The same records are seeded on both, so the two halves of the picture are the same words typed into the same box, one version each.

The test that covers this, and its result on this run: "Finding a customer by address, city or postal code still works" - https://shopview.testrail.io/index.php?/tests/view/2959359

SV-10061.title: Global Search: moving the mouse across the results changes which record Enter opens, and it stays changed
SV-10061.description: Type a word, press Enter, and one record opens. Do exactly the same again, but let the mouse pass over the list on its way somewhere else, and a different record opens - the one the pointer happened to cross. Nothing was clicked and nothing on screen says the target has moved. It stays moved after the pointer leaves the list, and it is still moved after the search is closed and opened again. Someone who types and presses Enter without looking down lands on a record they never chose.
steps: Sign in to the new version on the test branch: https://sv9160.qa.shopview.com
Click the search box at the top of the screen (or press Ctrl and K) and type Truck. A long list appears.
Without moving the mouse at all, press Enter. Write down which record opened.
Go back, open the search box again and type Truck a second time.
This time move the mouse down over the list until the pointer is over the ninth row - do NOT click - and then move the mouse away to the side, so it is not over any row.
Press Enter, and compare which record opens with the one you wrote down.
current: Without touching the mouse, Enter opened Desert Edge Truck Service & Repair.
After the pointer had crossed the list and moved away, Enter opened Henderson Mobile Truck Repair - the row the pointer passed over. Nobody clicked it.
The change sticks: the pointer is no longer over the list, and closing the search and opening it again on the same page leaves the same row as the one Enter will open.
expected: What Enter opens is set by what the person typed and by the arrow keys, and only changes when the person chooses - by arrowing to a row or by clicking it.
A pointer passing over the list on its way elsewhere does not change it, and nothing carries over after the search is closed and opened again.
SV-10061.shot_caption: The same word typed twice and Enter pressed both times. Above, the mouse was never touched. Below, the pointer had crossed the list and moved away - and a different record opens.
SV-10061.sources:
The panel says what drives it, in its own footer, read on the build on 15 September 2026: "Arrow down and arrow up navigate, Enter selects, Escape closes." It names the arrow keys and Enter, and it does not name the mouse.

Both halves of the picture are the new version on the test branch, on the same day and the same page - this is not a difference between the two versions, it is the new version behaving two different ways on the same words.

The test that covers this, and its result on this run: "Pressing Enter opens the top result without arrowing to it" - https://shopview.testrail.io/index.php?/tests/view/2980695

SV-10014.title: Global Search: a vehicle found by its VIN number is missing from the Assets section
SV-10014.description:
The search box says two things at once. The count along the top says the record has been found, and opening the Assets section says there are no results. Anyone who narrows down to the kind of record they are after - the natural thing to do - is told it does not exist. Only somebody who stays on All ever sees it.

One thing to know before reproducing it: this report's words name the VIN number BAHUTYV09T63EV7NS, while its own picture shows 0ED823VK8BWL1Y0MP typed into the box. Use the one in the picture.
steps: Sign in to the test branch: https://sv9160.qa.shopview.com
Click the search box at the top of the screen (or press Ctrl and K).
Type a vehicle VIN number - the report was raised on 0ED823VK8BWL1Y0MP, the 2016 Ram 2500 on 4 Star Truck Repair's list.
Read the number in brackets beside Assets along the top of the panel. It reads 1.
Click Assets, and read what the panel then lists.
current: The count beside Assets says 1, so the record was found.
Clicking Assets says there are no results.
The record is real: 2016 Ram 2500, on 4 Star Truck Repair.
expected: A record counted along the top is also listed when you click into its own section.
The check passes only when it shows in both.
SV-10014.shot_caption: What was seen: the count says the record is there, and the section says it is not.
SV-10014.sources:
What this is checked against is the new version's own panel: a number in brackets beside a section is a promise that clicking it will show that many records. This report is that the promise is broken.

There is no comparison with the version people use today, and there cannot be: the old search shows a plain list with a heading over each kind of record - it has no counts along the top and no section to click into. What this report is about only exists in the new version.

The check that covers this behaviour directly is "Selecting a scope tab shows only that entity's results with its count", https://shopview.testrail.io/index.php?/tests/view/2723892 - it has not been run yet.

The check for finding the record at all: "Selecting each result type opens the right record" - https://shopview.testrail.io/index.php?/tests/view/2738734

SV-10056.title: Global Search: a newly created job is not findable by its number for about 85 seconds
SV-10056.description:
A job you have just created cannot be found by its number for about 85 seconds. Other new records appear far sooner - a customer in 17 seconds, a part sale in 9 - so this is specific to jobs. No page reload and no signing out is involved: the job does appear on its own, it is simply very late.

It should be findable within 30 seconds.
steps: Sign in to the test branch: https://sv9160.qa.shopview.com
Open Work Orders and create a new job for any customer that has a vehicle. Write its number down.
Without reloading the page, click the search box at the top of the screen (or press Ctrl and K) and type that number.
If nothing comes back, clear the box, type it again, and keep an eye on the clock.
For comparison, create a new customer and a new part sale and time those the same way.
current: The job cannot be found for about 85 seconds.
A new customer is findable after about 17 seconds and a new part sale after about 9.
The job does appear in the end, with no reload and no signing out.
expected: A job you have just created is findable by its number within 30 seconds, with no page reload and no signing out.
The version people use today had no delay worth noticing, so anything close to the 30 seconds is already slower than what a service writer was used to.
SV-10056.shot_caption: The number of a newly created job typed into the search box, and the job coming back.
SV-10056.sources:
The 30 seconds comes from the Global Search Product Requirements, Confluence page 576978945, version 1.5, section 9: "Index refresh latency <= 30s for entity create/update." Section 8 adds that creating a record counts as viewing it, so it should be available straight away to the person who made it.

The check that covers this: "A new work order or part sale is findable within 30 seconds" - https://shopview.testrail.io/index.php?/tests/view/2959364

SV-10059.title: Global Search: the recently viewed list does not come back after a search that finds nothing
SV-10059.description: Open the search box without typing and a list of recently viewed things is shown, ready to click. Type something that matches nothing and the panel shows only a message. Clear the box again and the list does not come back - the person is left with nothing to click and has to close the search and open it again.
steps: Sign in to the test branch: https://sv9160.qa.shopview.com
Click the search box at the top of the screen (or press Ctrl and K) without typing anything. A list of recently viewed things is shown.
Type something that matches nothing at all, for example zzzqqqxxx, and read what the panel shows.
Clear the box completely.
Read what the panel shows now.
current: Typing something that matches nothing shows a message and nothing else, which is right.
Clearing the box leaves the panel empty - the recently viewed list does not return.
expected: After a search that finds nothing, clearing the box brings the recently viewed list back, so there is still something to click.
SV-10059.shot_caption: What was seen: a search that matched nothing, with nothing listed underneath it.
SV-10059.sources:
What this is checked against is the new version's own design: the list is shown when the box is empty, so emptying the box should show it again.

There is no comparison with the version people use today: its search box shows nothing at all when you open it without typing - it has no recently viewed list. The list is something the new version adds. Read on the live product on 15 September 2026.

The check that covers this: "Your recent items come back when a search finds nothing" - https://shopview.testrail.io/index.php?/tests/view/2981982

SV-10109.title: Global Search: a Vendor cannot be found by their address line 2, although a customer can
SV-10109.description: A company's address can run to two lines - a dock, a bay, a suite - and the second line is often the only part that tells two units on the same estate apart. The new search reads that second line on a CUSTOMER and ignores it on a VENDOR. Someone holding a delivery note with the bay number on it can find the customer and not the Vendor, from the same box, with the same kind of words. On the version people use today, both come back.
steps: Sign in to the new version on the test branch: https://sv9160.qa.shopview.com
Click the search box at the top of the screen (or press Ctrl and K), type ZZAUTOTEST Kestrel, and open that Vendor from the Vendors group. This also shows the search box itself is working.
On the Vendor's page, read the line marked Address 2. It says Bay 12C.
Open the search box again and type Bay 12C exactly as the record prints it.
Read the Vendors group and look for ZZAUTOTEST Kestrel Parts Supply.
Now clear the box and type Dock 7B - the address line 2 of the customer ZZAUTOTEST Bridgeport Hauling - and read the Customers group. This is the same kind of search on the other kind of company.
current: The Vendor is not returned. The one company listed under Vendors is B&K Truck Repair LLC, which is offered because its NAME looks a little like the words typed - its address has nothing to do with them.
The customer search in the same sitting works: typing Dock 7B returns ZZAUTOTEST Bridgeport Hauling.
The Vendor comes straight back when its name is typed, so the record is there and the search box is working, and its own page shows Address 2: Bay 12C, so the field is filled in.
expected: The Vendor whose address line 2 was typed is returned, under Vendors - the same way the customer already is under Customers.
This is what the version people use today does.
SV-10109.shot_caption: The same address line typed into both versions. Above, the live product returns the Vendor. Below, the new version returns an unrelated company matched on its name.
SV-10109.sources:
The expected behaviour comes from the version people use today. It was not read out of a specification - it was typed into the live product at https://app.shopview.com on 15 September 2026, where Bay 12C returned ZZAUTOTEST Kestrel Parts Supply, and the picture above is that search. The Vendor's record on the live product shows the same Address 2, so the field is filled in on both. The same records are seeded on both, so the two halves of the picture are the same words typed into the same box, one version each.

Worth reading beside this one: the Vendor's postcode and the state it is in are not searched either, and those are already reported as SV-10005 and SV-10006. Measured field by field on 15 September, a Vendor is found by its name, its street and its town and by nothing else on its address; a customer is found by all of those plus its address line 2 and its state. It may be one piece of work rather than three.

The test that covers this, and its result on this run: "Finding a customer or vendor by address line 2" - https://shopview.testrail.io/index.php?/tests/view/2959370

SV-10031.title: Part Sales: a new part sale is created but the app cannot open it, and shows two errors
SV-10031.description:
Pressing Save on a new part sale shows two red messages and the part sale never opens. The record is not lost - it appears in the Part Sales list a moment later - but the person who just made it cannot get into it to add anything. They are left looking at an error, with no way of telling whether the thing they created exists or not.

It happened every time it was tried, and each attempt produced a different support reference, so it is not a one-off.
steps: Sign in to the test branch: https://sv9160.qa.shopview.com
Open Parts from the top menu, then Part Sales.
Click New Part Sale, at the top right.
In the New part sale box, choose a customer - 4 Star Truck Repair will do.
Click Save, and read what appears.
Close the messages and look at the Part Sales list.
current: Two red messages appear. The first says an error occurred and gives a support reference to quote. The second says the part sale you are trying to open does not exist.
The new part sale does not open.
It is in the list all the same - P9160-250, against 4 Star Truck Repair, with no parts on it and no total. So the record was made; the app just cannot reach it.
Trying again does the same thing, with a different support reference each time.
expected: Pressing Save creates the part sale and opens it, ready for parts to be added.
No error message appears.
SV-10031.shot_caption: Above, the two messages shown after pressing Save. Below, the part sales list a moment later, with the new one sitting in it.
SV-10031.sources:
There is no specification behind this one and none is needed: the New Part Sale button exists to create a part sale and open it, and it does neither cleanly. The proof that the record is really made is the list itself, in the picture above - so the failure is between creating it and opening it, not in the creating.

Seen on the test branch https://sv9160.qa.shopview.com, build v26.36.4-7869ff2, on 14 September 2026, signed in as an administrator, with a full screen recording attached. The support references from two of the attempts were 5bc49151-2dc2-4143-823f-115cb4fbc801 and dd7c7cbb-1b8f-4ab0-a4ca-5e13d91d75b1.

It has NOT been re-checked since. On 16 September the branch's sign-in changed - the quick sign-in used for testing is no longer offered and the page now asks for a Google account - so nobody has been able to try it again. Worth re-running the moment that is sorted out.
